title: sdks: unify auth/retries + streaming ergonomics across Python/TypeScript/Go; parity & v1.68.2 bumps
author: Ava Chen
release_notes:
- SDK parity fixes across Python/TypeScript/Go
- Unified auth/retry behavior for token refresh and exponential-backoff
- Streaming API ergonomics: consistent iterator/async iterator across SDKs
- Bump SDK package versions to v1.68.2
description:
Motivation: We maintain three language SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go) and have drifted in auth semantics, retry backoff, and streaming ergonomics. This PR unifies behavior across SDKs to reduce production inconsistencies and ease cross-language adoption.

What this PR does: Consolidates auth token refresh semantics (transparent background refresh + single inflight refresh suppression), standardizes retry policies (idempotency-aware default, jittered exponential backoff, configurable max attempts), and harmonizes streaming API ergonomics (sync/async iterator parity, consistent error propagation, and cancelation behavior). Also includes a set of small compatibility/parity fixes and bumps package versions to v1.68.2 across SDKs.

Compatibility: Changes are backwards-compatible for the majority of users. The default retry policy is slightly more conservative for safety (retries moved from 5 -> 4 for non-idempotent requests), but can be overridden by passing the previous config. Streaming API preserves existing call signatures but improves iterator behavior for partial reads; see upgrade notes below.

Upgrade notes: - Python: update to redwood==1.68.2; explicit retry config is supported via Client(retries=...). - TypeScript: @redwood/sdk v1.68.2; streaming now exposes asyncIterator() helper for easier for-await usage. - Go: client option RetryConfig and StreamContext support added; bump to v1.68.2.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement core auth/retry changes in each SDK
- [x] Add unit & integration tests for streaming behavior
- [x] Update docs and changelog
- [x] Run cross-SDK compatibility tests

Related: ENG-4312 (auth parity), ENG-4380 (retries), ENG-4401 (streaming ergonomics).
